source: Chapter 1.pdf, The Wonderful World of Science, reprint 2026-27
method: Map visible printed teaching points, not the PDF's duplicated hidden text layer. Source production marks, watermark, QR link, running furniture and decorative slogans are not lesson requirements.

points.point: Childhood curiosity develops into studying science in Class 6; science involves observing, thinking and doing.
Science spans grains of sand, mountains, grass, forests, oceans, space and everyday places.
Questions about stars and flowers can begin an investigation.
New discoveries add knowledge, reveal new questions and sometimes revise earlier explanations; unfinished-puzzle analogy.
Ideas in science are connected and useful in daily life.
Earth supports diverse life; protect its environments; explore growth of plants and animals.
Explore food and ingredients in India's varied cuisines.
Explore water, rain, ice, vapour and temperature measurement.
Compare everyday materials, magnets, uses and separation.
Explore motion, leaves, seeds and questions about the Sun, Moon and stars.
Stopped-pen example: ask why, suggest empty refill, inspect, reconsider if ink remains.
Activity 1.1: describe a problem you solved and the steps you took.
Scientific method: observe, question, suggest an answer, test through experiments or observations, analyse results.
Anyone can use scientific reasoning; examples of cook, bicycle repairer and electrician.
Activity 1.2: describe a daily-life example of someone following a scientific method.
Curiosity and careful observation strengthen the ability to investigate larger questions.
Activity 1.3: ask a Why question and plan how to seek an answer.
Scientists collaborate in teams; friends can help investigate.
Some answers come beyond Grade 6, over the next five years and later.
Continue exploring and asking questions.

editorialDecisions: Use the established Science V2 Source Serif 4/Source Sans 3 typography and natural right edges, superseding the older Science profile's Spectral/Poppins and justified setting.
Use Chapter 1's blue identity with the V2 full-width opener and matched magnifier motifs; teal Investigate and amber Think It Through retain their V2 roles.
Preserve all three source reflection tasks as substantial unnumbered Think It Through boxes. No textbook writing spaces.
Add two safe first-hand tasks: observation and paper-folding comparison. Setup never specifies a required result.
Distinguish hypothesis, prediction and observation; bound the pen-refill test by visibility. Do not imply that seeing remaining ink identifies the actual fault.
Introduce fair comparisons, repeat tests and limits of conclusions using an accessible example. The method diagram is a guide, not a universal rigid sequence.
Keep glossary and summary together on one dedicated reference page because both are short; add six assessment questions aligned to the new reading copy.

Extract source illustrations at native resolution and use small print widths; copy the existing high-resolution opener independently. Pen, method and topic diagrams use live vector geometry and labels.
